introduction: Tharnadia’s expedition and a cloaked figure seek proof from the Old Quarter and Braddistock. Three cards track armoury clearance, the necromancer’s remains and a local spirit’s release. Keys, the cathedral, buried treasure and the larger retaking story add separate leads. Discovery is separate; new progress requires active, ready accounting.
orientation: ASK LEADER about hi, old, quarter, braddistock or cathedral. ASK CLOAKED about hi, quest, braddistock, mansion, old or quarter. They describe competing purposes, but accept the same five kinds for armoury access. Choose either recipient for that offering; each has a separate native receipt, within one journal story.

Armoury clearance needs the remains of Lord Braddistock, the mansion’s former master, the warrior guildmaster, the mage guildmaster and the rogue guildmaster. Carry one of each loose. The four Old Quarter remains share broad names, so check their identities carefully. Five copies of one kind cannot replace five different kinds.

Braddistock’s lead follows a silver key, the chained jaguar’s collar and the lord’s accepted return. The four other proofs are declared on different Old Quarter foes. These are source leads: matching items supplied by another player fit the Tharnadian offering without separately proving who fought, recovered them first or freed those spirits.

The shiny armoury key leads to the Old Quarter armoury. The necromancer stands at its entrance, while his requested remains are separately declared on the armoury floor. Carry those exact remains loose to either the leader or the cloaked figure for the gate key. This accepted return does not require a recorded earlier clearance, despite the dialogue’s larger sequence.

The gate key is used on the route through the Twin Keeps. Holding a key, opening a shared door and entering an area are different events. A key may also be found in the leader’s pouch. Neither key possession nor an accepted proof return records that the keeps were investigated or Tharnadia retaken.

A small black key in a ruined bedroom belongs to the spirit at the old rack. Return that exact item loose to the spirit for experience; the native return makes the spirit depart. Its accepted receipt is separate from the banker’s safe key, an ordinary corpse, a personal first recovery or permanent peace for the city.

The cathedral uses an ethereal key associated with Lord Perrin at the Winterhaven Outpost. The skeletal knight’s skull opens the abbatoir container. The warning about a death howl needs gameplay qualification: the current special procedure and engine dispatch disagree. This journal cannot promise that the warning triggers, that surviving it is recorded or that the cathedral is cleared.

The banker’s safe, directional tunnel keys, secret trapdoor, old coins, tracks, ruined weapons and shadowrift provide other exploration leads. Their shared state and actual outcomes are separate from these three accepted stories. Optional material rows show loose supplies now; accepted history remains after they are spent. Alternative recipients share one achievement and one potential daily per story, without guaranteeing admitted stock.

contacts.name: the leader of the expeditionary force
contacts.description: Explains the expedition’s Old Quarter, Braddistock and cathedral leads. Accepts five distinct remains for the armoury key, or exact necromancer remains for the gate key.

contacts.name: a mysterious cloaked humanoid
contacts.description: Offers an alternative recipient for the same five-proof clearance and necromancer return. His purpose and eventual departure differ from the expedition’s; neither creates a second journal unit for the same story.

contacts.name: the spirit of a slack-jawed prostitute
contacts.description: Accepts the exact small black key for experience and departs. This spirit is a separate local return, without an advertised ASK topic.

contacts.name: a fifty foot skeletal knight
contacts.description: Carries the skull used as the abbatoir key. His feared howl has a source dispatch mismatch requiring qualification; encounter, combat, skull recovery and container access remain separate.

contacts.name: the spirit of Sarn, the banker
contacts.description: Carries the bank safe key. His appearance and the safe’s shared contents are exploration context, without a selected native quest return.
